newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-SWISS DELIGHT AFTER IMPORTANT WORLD CUP SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWISS DELIGHT AFTER IMPORTANT WORLD CUP SUCCESS.

text.p: It would have been no surprise if Swiss soccer fans had flown their own red flags high in Zurich's May Day celebrations on Thursday after their country's 1-0 World Cup victory over Hungary on Wednesday. Failure to win would have left Hungary as the only realistic challengers to the group three leaders Norway but Kubilay Turkyilmaz's late goal took Switzerland into second place above the Hungarians, adding to the importance of the return game in Budapest in August.
Norway lead the group with 10 points from four matches, followed by Switzerland and Hungary on six points, Finland (4) and Azerbaijan (3).

So Switzerland's victory was absolutely vital and won over some of those who had been doubting coach Rolf Fringer -- hardly a great success since replacing Artur Jorge after last summer's European Championship finals.

Fringer had put his reputation -- and, some critics felt, his job -- on the line by changing to a 4-3-3 system, moving team captain Ciriaco Sforza into defence and introdcing the national team's youngest-ever midfield. At the same time he also publically demanded greater commitment from his more experienced players.

The response was impressive, and the multi-lingual squad spoke afterwards with one voice about discipline, patience and the rewards of hard work. Raphael Wicky, 20, one of the young midfield trio said: "We've seen the proof that the coach made exactly the right choice with his 4-4-3 lineup. It also confirmed that if you put in a lot of effort you win."
Fringer must now decide whether to continue with three attackers match in Budapest, especially if Hungary move three points ahead of the Swiss by beating group leaders Norway next month.
Even the coach admitted: "To win the group will still be very difficult."
At least the standing of Austrian citizen Fringer is now considerably higher than it was when Switzerland lost to Azerbaijan last August.
But despite the improvements made since then, that defeat could yet undermine the Swiss challenge.
